chapters.summary: Council staff announces the hearing of the Subcommittee on Zoning and Franchises, asks attendees to silence devices and not approach the dais.
chapters.title: Council staff opens hearing with housekeeping announcements

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Good morning and welcome to today's New York City Council hearing on the Committee of Zoning and Franchises.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: At this time, please silence all electronic devices.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: No one may approach the dais.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Chair, you may begin.

chapters.summary: Chair Farah N. Louis convenes the subcommittee, introduces members present (Farias, Encarnacion, Sanchez, Thomas-Henry, Minority Leader Carr), and outlines the agenda: three votes and six hearings.
chapters.title: Chair Louis convenes subcommittee and outlines agenda

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Good morning and welcome to a meeting of the Subcommittee on Zoning and Franchises.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: I am Councilmember Farrah Lewis, Chair of the Subcommittee.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: This morning, we are joined by Councilmembers Farias and Canacion, Jay Sanchez, Thomas Henry, Minority Leader Carr.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Today, we are voting on three proposals and holding six hearings.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: The scheduled vote for LUs 123 and 124 regarding the 158-06 Northern Boulevard rezoning is laid over.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: The three proposals that we will vote on are 815 Hutchinson River Parkway, Commercial Rezoning and Councilmember Aldebals District,

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: 862-868 Kent Avenue, Mixed-Use Residential Rezoning and Councilmember Restless District, 132 Melrose Street, Mixed-Use Residential Rezoning and Councilmember Gutierrez's District.

chapters.summary: Chair Louis lists the six hearing items: Park Avenue, 289 Kent Avenue, Fort Hamilton Mews, 21-31 46th Avenue, and Sojourner Truth MAPES rezoning proposals across Brooklyn, Queens, and the Bronx.
chapters.title: Chair Louis lists six rezoning hearings scheduled

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: We will then hold the hearings on the following proposals.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: 69-67108 Street Rezoning, Mixed-Use Residential Rezoning in Councilmember Shulman's District, Park Avenue Mixed-Use Residential Rezoning in Councilmember Restless District, 289 Kent Avenue Mixed-Use Residential Rezoning in Councilmember Restless District,

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Use residential rezoning and council member wrestlers district 21-3146th Avenue mixed use rezone residential rezoning and council member Juan's district.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: 289 Kent Avenue Mixed-Use Residential Rezoning in Councilmember Restless District,

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Fort Hamilton Muse, mixed-use residential rezoning and Councilmember Santosuoso's district, and Sojourner Truth MAPES, mixed-use residential rezoning and Councilmember Felice's district.

chapters.summary: Chair Louis explains the hybrid format, registration process for remote and in-person testimony, two-minute time limit, written testimony submission, and decorum rules for the hearing.
chapters.title: Chair Louis explains hybrid format and testimony rules

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: This meeting is being held in hybrid format.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Members of the public who wish to testify may testify in person or via Zoom.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Members of the public wishing to testify remotely may register by visiting the New York City Council website at www.council.nyc.gov backslash land use.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: To sign up or for those of you here in person, please see one of the sergeant at arms to prepare and submit a speaker card.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Members of the public may also view a live stream broadcast of the meeting at the council's website.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: When you are called to testify before the subcommittee, if you are joining us remotely, you will remain muted until recognized by myself to speak.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: When you are recognized, your microphone will be unmuted.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: We will limit public testimony to two minutes per witness.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: If you have additional testimony that you would like the subcommittee to consider, or if you have written testimony that you would like to submit instead of appearing in person, please email it to landyousetestimony at council.nyc.gov.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Written testimony must be submitted up to three days after the hearing is closed.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Please indicate the LU number and or project name in the subject line of your email.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: We request that witnesses joining us remotely remain in the meeting until excused by the chair, as council members may have questions.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Lastly, for everyone attending today's meeting, this is a government proceeding and decorum must be observed at all times.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Members of the public are asked to speak during the meeting unless you are testifying.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: The witness table is reserved for people who are called to testify and no video recording or photography is allowed from the witness table.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Further, members of the public may not.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Present audio or video recordings as testimony, but may submit transcripts of such recordings to the sergeant at arms for inclusion in the hearing record.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: We will now proceed with the three votes.

chapters.summary: Chair Louis describes LU 120, the 815 Hutchinson River Parkway commercial rezoning in the Bronx, seeking to allow large retail establishments (10,000+ sq ft) by changing M1-2 to C8-3. Councilmember Audible supports.
chapters.title: Chair Louis describes 815 Hutchinson River Parkway vote proposal

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: The first vote concerns L.U.'s 120 regarding the 815 Hutchinson River Parkway commercial rezoning proposal in Councilmember Audible's district.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Applicant is seeking to allow large retail establishments of 10,000 square feet or larger at an existing commercial center in the Ferry Point neighborhood of the Bronx.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: The proposal is a zoning map amendment to change the existing manufacturing N1-2 district to a commercial C8-3 district.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Councilmember Audible supports this application.

chapters.summary: Chair Louis describes LUs 121-122, the 862-868 Kent Avenue mixed-use residential rezoning in Williamsburg, Brooklyn, seeking ~74 apartments with ~19 affordable. Councilmember Restler supports.
chapters.title: Chair Louis describes 862-868 Kent Avenue vote proposal

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: The second vote concerns LUs 121 and 122 regarding the 862-86.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: A Kent Avenue mixed-use residential rezoning proposal in Councilmember Restler's district.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Applicant is seeking to develop a mixed-use residential project in Williamsburg, Brooklyn, that would have approximately 74 apartments, of which approximately 19 apartments will be permanently affordable.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: The proposal involves two actions.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: The first is a zoning map amendment to change the existing manufacturing M1-1 district to a mixed-use district.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Consisting of a paired M1-4 district with a residential R6A district.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: The second action is a zoning tax amendment to map a mandatory inclusionary housing area.

chapters.summary: Chair Louis describes LUs 125-126, the 132 Melrose Street rezoning in Bushwick, Brooklyn, seeking ~18 apartments with ~5 affordable. A modification removes MIH Option 2 to ensure 60% AMI average. Councilmember Gutierrez supports as modified.
chapters.title: Chair Louis describes 132 Melrose Street vote proposal with modification

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Councilmember Ressler supports this application.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: The third and final vote concerns LUs 125 and 126 regarding 132 Melrose Street mixed-use residential rezoning proposal in Councilmember Gutierrez's district.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Applicant is seeking to develop a mixed-use residential project in Bushwick, Brooklyn.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: That would have approximately 18 apartments, of which approximately five apartments would be permanently affordable.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: The proposal involves two actions.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: The first is a zoning map amendment to change the existing manufacturing M1-1 district to a mixed-use district consisting of a paired M1-2A district with a residential R6A district.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: The second action is a zoning tax amendment to map a mandatory inclusionary housing.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: We are recommending one modification to remove MIH option two, which will ensure the affordable apartments are provided at an average of 60% AMI.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Councilmember Gutierrez supports this application as modified.

chapters.summary: Chair Louis asks if any council members have questions or remarks on the vote items. No members have questions, and the chair stands at ease before calling the vote.
chapters.title: Chair Louis calls for questions before vote

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Council, are there any members, any council members with questions or remarks at this time?

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: No, Chair.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Members appearing remotely who have questions, remarks about today's items should use the raise hand button.

chapters.summary: Chair Louis calls for a vote to approve LU 120 and LUs 121-122, and to approve with modification LUs 125-126. Council staff conducts the roll call.

utterances.text: Stand at ease.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: I will now call for a vote to approve LU 120 related to the 815 Hutchinson River Parkway

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: rezoning proposal and LUs 121 and 122 related to the 862-868 Kent Avenue rezoning proposal to approve with modification LUs 125 and 126

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: related to the 132 Melrose Street rezoning proposal.

chapters.summary: Chair Louis opens the hearing on pre-considered LUs for the Park Avenue Brooklyn mixed-use residential rezoning in Bed-Stuy, Council Member Restler's district. The proposal would create 391 apartments with ~117 affordable and four community facility buildings for private educational uses.
chapters.title: Park Avenue Brooklyn rezoning hearing opens

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: I will now open the hearing on pre-considered LUs regarding Park Avenue, Brooklyn, a mixed-use residential rezoning proposal, and Bed-Stuy, Brooklyn, and Council Member Restless District.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Applicant, which consists of multiple owners over five adjacent blocks, is seeking to develop mixed-use residential buildings that would have a total of 391 apartments,

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: and four of the buildings would have community facility space for private educational uses.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Mandatory inclusionary housing would be mapped as part of the application, which would require that up to approximately 117 of the apartments be permanently affordable.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: For anyone wishing to testify regarding this proposal remotely, if you have not already done so, you must register online by visiting the council's website at council.nyc.gov backslash land use.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: For anyone with us in person, please see one of the sergeant at arms to submit a speaker card.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: If you would prefer to submit written testimony, you can always do so by emailing landusestestimony at council.nyc.gov.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: We now recognize council.

chapters.summary: Council Member Restler describes the five-year history of the Park Avenue rezoning, originally proposed to add school capacity and legalize yeshivas in South Williamsburg and Bed-Stuy. He criticizes DOT's environmental review process for delaying the project and praises the delivery of 2,500 yeshiva seats.
chapters.title: Council Member Restler remarks on Park Avenue rezoning history and yeshiva capacity

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: So, Member Ressa, four remarks.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Just asking which of the projects it was this morning.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: So thank you so much, Chair Lewis, for your great leadership of this committee.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: It is always a pleasure to be with you.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: When I, before I took office in 2021, community leaders from across South Williamsburg and Bed-Stuy asked me to meet about a critically important rezoning.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: And it was proposed at the time as a handful of individual sites that would add housing, but more importantly, more urgently, add school capacity for

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: for the community in South Williamsburg and Bed-Stuy and legalize existing yeshivas and build new yeshivas that could really meet the needs of the community.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: I hear from families in South Williamsburg and Bed-Stuy every single week who tell me that they're struggling to find affordable housing and the yeshivas are bursting at the seams and that we need more

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: capacity for both.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: And it's been a winding, painful, frustrating process to get us here some five years later, literally.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: But we're at the finish line of what is a critically important development.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: project for the future of the Jewish community in South Williamsburg.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: And I am enormously grateful, particularly the yeshiva administrators, and I see some of them here with me today, who have diligently fought hard to make sure that this stays on track and gets done.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: The Department of City Planning insisted that this be one zoning application rather than a handful of individual applications, which then set off a series of implications around community investments that this development team would need to make.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: And, you know, I always welcome community investments.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: That's my job is to try to see those out every time at every opportunity.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: But this development proposal in and of itself is a tremendous community investment by adding literally 2,500 yeshiva seats to our community.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: So I'm glad, and I will just say one more thing, that I was already a critic of the environmental review process, but watching the Department of Transportation and the Department of Parks and Recreation, but especially DOT,

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: butcher the environmental review process and just enact their own policy agenda to have this development team go through hell was infuriating.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: We lost years on this project because of the Department of Transportation's intransigence.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: And I really, truly hope that Commissioner Flynn will whip the environmental review team into shape at DOT because what they have been doing is disgraceful.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: That being said, I am thrilled that this proposal is before the council and moving forward and would welcome a very, very, very, very brief presentation from the applicant.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Thank you, Councilmember Ressler.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: I will now call the applicant panel for this proposal, which consists of Benjamin Stark.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Council, can you please administer the oath?

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Can you please raise your right hand and state your name for record?

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Ben Stark, do you expect to tell the truth and nothing but the truth in your testimony this morning in response to council member questions?

utterances.speaker: Benjamin Stark
utterances.text: Yes, I do, counsel.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: You may now begin your testimony, which is limited to 10 minutes, and you should start to conclude your presentation after eight minutes.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: When you begin your presentation, please restate your name and the name of your organization, and you may begin.

chapters.summary: Benjamin Stark of Hershkin Singer Epstein presents the Park Avenue Rezoning Partners application, a coalition of property owners and Jewish educational institutions seeking to rezone five blocks of legacy manufacturing zoning along Park Avenue to deliver school seats and affordable housing.
chapters.title: Applicant Stark introduces Park Avenue rezoning team and purpose

utterances.speaker: Benjamin Stark
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair Lewis.

utterances.speaker: Benjamin Stark
utterances.text: My name is Benjamin Stark.

utterances.speaker: Benjamin Stark
utterances.text: I'm a partner at Hershen Singer Epstein for the applicant Park Avenue Rezoning Partners.

utterances.speaker: Benjamin Stark
utterances.text: Right off the bat, just the deepest thanks.

utterances.speaker: Benjamin Stark
utterances.text: Really, words can't express the thanks that this applicant team has.

utterances.speaker: Benjamin Stark
utterances.text: It's not the support of Councilmember Ressler.

utterances.speaker: Benjamin Stark
utterances.text: It's the commitment of Councilmember Ressler to recognizing very early in this process the deep community benefit of this application.

utterances.speaker: Benjamin Stark
utterances.text: And being a partner in that advocacy from every step of the way.

utterances.speaker: Benjamin Stark
utterances.text: Really, the words...

utterances.speaker: Benjamin Stark
utterances.text: that I'm saying right now cannot capture the gratitude that this community feels for that degree of leadership and really just being

utterances.speaker: Benjamin Stark
utterances.text: at the forefront of understanding why there's need here and what needs to get done to deliver on that need.

utterances.speaker: Benjamin Stark
utterances.text: So without that further ado, I'll get to this presentation.

utterances.speaker: Benjamin Stark
utterances.text: I will make every effort to keep it brief.

utterances.speaker: Benjamin Stark
utterances.text: As it was introduced, this is an application by a coalition of property owners and Jewish educational institutions with very deep roots in the South Williamsburg and Bedford-Stuyvesant communities.

utterances.speaker: Benjamin Stark
utterances.text: They're seeking to rezone five blocks of a legacy 1961-era manufacturing district along Park Avenue,

utterances.speaker: Benjamin Stark
utterances.text: zoning that no longer reflects how this neighborhood lives, works, or grows in order to deliver two urgent public benefits, the aforementioned school seats and affordable housing.

utterances.speaker: Benjamin Stark
utterances.text: This is not a conventional rezoning.

utterances.speaker: Benjamin Stark
utterances.text: There's no single developer or property owner behind it.

utterances.speaker: Benjamin Stark
utterances.text: Park Avenue Rezoning Partners is a group of property owners and educational institutions.

utterances.speaker: Benjamin Stark
utterances.text: Next slide, please.

utterances.speaker: Benjamin Stark
utterances.text: The Beth Chana School, Central United Talmudical Academy, Yeshivas of Ahavas Israel, Yeshiva Litziram Satmar, institutions that have served South Williamsburg community for decades.

utterances.speaker: Benjamin Stark
utterances.text: They're educational and spiritual anchors of this neighborhood, and they share a common problem, a serious problem, that the zoning has not kept pace with the community that they serve, a community that has been and will continue to grow exponentially.

utterances.speaker: Benjamin Stark
utterances.text: The owners of the residential sites in this application are not controlled by outside investors.

utterances.speaker: Benjamin Stark
utterances.text: They are owned by outside investors.

utterances.speaker: Benjamin Stark
utterances.text: community members, and community affiliate entities who have also been on these blocks for years.

utterances.speaker: Benjamin Stark
utterances.text: This application addresses community needs in a single coordinated framework, and it does so without displacing a single existing resident.

chapters.summary: Stark details the project benefits: over 2,500 school seats across four educational facilities, approximately 390 new dwelling units with 98-117 permanently affordable, and new ground floor retail along Park Avenue with commitment to retain existing tenants.
chapters.title: Applicant Stark details school seats, housing, and retail benefits

utterances.speaker: Benjamin Stark
utterances.text: If approved, this rezoning will deliver, as the council member mentioned, over 2,500 school seats across four educational facilities.

utterances.speaker: Benjamin Stark
utterances.text: Approximately 390 new dwelling units with between 98 and 117 permanently affordable pursuant to MIH, an expansive new ground floor retail presence along Park Avenue with commitment from the applicants to try and retain existing tenants.

utterances.speaker: Benjamin Stark
utterances.text: Next slide, please.

utterances.speaker: Benjamin Stark
utterances.text: So where are we?

utterances.speaker: Benjamin Stark
utterances.text: The project area straddles Park Avenue between Bedford Avenue generally to the west and Notion Avenue to the east, south of Flushing, north of Myrtle Avenue.

utterances.speaker: Benjamin Stark
utterances.text: This is a transition zone between South Williamsburg and Bedford-Stuyvesant, and we are within the inner transit zone.

utterances.speaker: Benjamin Stark
utterances.text: Next slide, please.

utterances.speaker: Benjamin Stark
utterances.text: Why are we here?

utterances.speaker: Benjamin Stark
utterances.text: The problem speaks for itself.

utterances.speaker: Benjamin Stark
utterances.text: This is a community, the project serves a community with a school-age population that is undergoing tremendous growth, especially amongst its youngest cohorts.

utterances.speaker: Benjamin Stark
utterances.text: In this community, a very large percentage of children attend private religious schools, and many families have...

utterances.speaker: Benjamin Stark
utterances.text: Many children, between six and ten children.

utterances.speaker: Benjamin Stark
utterances.text: The needs for schools is acute presently, but the real important message we need to deliver is that the problem will only grow as the years and decades go by.

utterances.speaker: Benjamin Stark
utterances.text: Next slide, please.

utterances.speaker: Benjamin Stark
utterances.text: Similarly, this problem is multifaceted.

utterances.speaker: Benjamin Stark
utterances.text: The issues with affordable housing in this city, in this borough, don't need any introduction, but the issues with affordable housing in particular within Community District 3 is also acute.

utterances.speaker: Benjamin Stark
utterances.text: This application serves in part to address that need.

utterances.speaker: Benjamin Stark
utterances.text: Next slide.

utterances.speaker: Benjamin Stark
utterances.text: What does the Park Avenue rezoning do in that regard?

utterances.speaker: Benjamin Stark
utterances.text: It will seek to legalize existing educational uses and allow for the development of new, sorely needed educational facilities with the development of new housing and affordable housing in this growing residential community

utterances.speaker: Benjamin Stark
utterances.text: where the legacy zoning just simply no longer reflects what is happening on the ground.

chapters.summary: Stark explains the spatial logic of the rezoning: mid-density M1-4/R7D along Park Avenue for residential buildings, with school sites on side streets positioned for coordinated school safety and operational considerations.
chapters.title: Applicant Stark explains zoning spatial logic and school siting

utterances.speaker: Benjamin Stark
utterances.text: Next slide, please.

utterances.speaker: Benjamin Stark
utterances.text: So how are we positioning this?

utterances.speaker: Benjamin Stark
utterances.text: What you see up on the slide, we're going to kind of walk through the spatial logic of this.

utterances.speaker: Benjamin Stark
utterances.text: Park Avenue itself, running right down the center, within 100 feet of the street line on both sides, is proposed to be zoned to a mid-density M14R7D district.

utterances.speaker: Benjamin Stark
utterances.text: This is where the residential buildings will go.

utterances.speaker: Benjamin Stark
utterances.text: This is one of the wonderful coincidences of this application is that site control by the schools was...

utterances.speaker: Benjamin Stark
utterances.text: Within proximity of other schools.

utterances.speaker: Benjamin Stark
utterances.text: You see the school sites here, B, C, H, and G.

utterances.speaker: Benjamin Stark
utterances.text: They are coincidentally opposite the side streets from one another.

utterances.speaker: Benjamin Stark
utterances.text: It allows this proposal to have a coordinated

utterances.speaker: Benjamin Stark
utterances.text: when it comes to school safety and other operational considerations, again, underscoring the appropriateness of this particular micro-neighborhood for the proposal that's before you today.

utterances.speaker: Benjamin Stark
utterances.text: The mid-blocks that you see there, they are deep, long lots that the schools require for their particular uses.

utterances.speaker: Benjamin Stark
utterances.text: Imagine some of you on the board are understanding of the challenges of citing new schools and need for sort of minimum sizing on floor plates.

utterances.speaker: Benjamin Stark
utterances.text: It's exceptionally challenging to find school sites.

utterances.text: We're here to, as Council Member Ressler mentioned,

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: and to rezone a vestigial 1961 zoning M31 heavy manufacturing site that has not been operated as a heavy manufacturing site in decades.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: That three tax lots within the rezoning area would be rezoned to allow for residential use, including a significant amount of affordable housing, and a portion of the block, which has remained M31

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: since 1961 but has never operated as such, will be zoned to M12A to allow for a wider variety of uses.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: In addition, as I mentioned, the portion of the rezoning area that will allow for residential use will be mapped as MIH.

chapters.summary: Cozen describes the site's excellent transit access (L train, J/Z/M, ferry), proximity to Domino Park and other open spaces, and the surrounding context of tall waterfront buildings with a policy of gradually less dense development moving east.
chapters.title: Applicant Cozen on site location, transit, and surrounding context

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: Next slide, please.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: So the site is located on the east side of Kent Avenue between South 1st and South 2nd Streets.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: It has excellent transit, and the location is very advantageous for transit.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: It's within about a half a mile from the L train as well as the JZM and a ferry stop along the waterfront.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: There are significant open spaces including Domino Park, William Sheridan Playground, and various other hopefully soon to be built open space resources as part of River Ring.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: Next slide, please.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: As Council Member Ressler noted, there are significant either already built or soon to be built buildings along the waterfront to the west of Kent Avenue.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: The city has adopted a policy in this area that they would like to see development gradually become less dense and have smaller envelopes as you move east in Williamsburg.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: And Toby will speak to that more later on in the presentation.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: Next slide, please.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: So walking around the site, you can see in the top left-hand corner, looking south on Kent, you can see the domino buildings that were built when this picture was taken.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: On the top right-hand corner, you can see there is an existing, I believe it's 10-story building that is a pre-existing non-con...

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: Actually, no, it is a former ink factory that was converted to residential pursuant to a variance.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: The site is a...

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: warehouse, the building on the development site right now is a warehouse that has a temporary storage use.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: It has not been actively used by any tenant since Vice Media left.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: Next slide, please.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: As I mentioned, on the left-hand side, you can see the existing M31 zoning district.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: On the right-hand side, you can see the portions in pink and purple that will be rezoned to M13A-R7X, as well as the smaller portion along Wythe Avenue and South 2nd that will be rezoned to M12A.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: Next slide, please.

chapters.summary: Cozen presents the illustrative massing: approximately 17 floors with ground floor retail, 278 dwelling units with 56-83 affordable depending on MIH option, and a voluntary 10-foot sidewalk widening along Kent Avenue.
chapters.title: Applicant Cozen on building massing and unit count

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: This is an illustrative massing of the building that the applicant intends to develop.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: It's approximately 17 floors in height with ground floor retail, open spaces along, you know, Kent Avenue, South 1st and South 2nd.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: The applicant is also voluntarily widening the sidewalk along Kent Avenue 10 feet so that there's greater pedestrian circulation space in an area that it is much needed.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: The building will have approximately 278 dwelling units, depending on the option, the MIH option, a significant amount of which will be affordable.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: I believe that's between 56 and 83, depending on the option selected.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: Next slide, please.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: And this is a slide of the illustrative massing in context with the larger river ring buildings to be developed as well as the domino buildings.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: There is one domino building that is on the east side of Kent, and that is approximately 175 feet tall in height, and that is what the city has determined is an appropriate height and density for the east side of Kent Avenue.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: As Toby will, I'll hand it over to Toby.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: He'll explain kind of how that sloping density and height has played out.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: Next slide, please.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: Oh, this is one more massing.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: Next slide.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: This slide after that, please.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Toby Snyder of FX Collaborative presents the design approach: transitional massing between waterfront towers and smaller grain fabric, broken into smaller pieces with masonry materials, sidewalk widening, and rooftop amenities including solar canopy.
chapters.title: Architect Snyder presents 289 Kent Avenue design and massing approach

utterances.speaker: Toby Snyder
utterances.text: Hello, I'm Toby Snyder, Principal and Design Director at FX Collaborative Architects.

utterances.speaker: Toby Snyder
utterances.text: Yeah, the massing we're seeking here is transitional.

utterances.speaker: Toby Snyder
utterances.text: As Council Member Ressler mentioned, there's, of course, tall towers on the west side of Kent Avenue and then smaller grain fabric on the eastern side.

utterances.speaker: Toby Snyder
utterances.text: And we seek for our site here, the white building in the center here, to be sort of part of, help this transition.

utterances.speaker: Toby Snyder
utterances.text: Next slide, please.

utterances.speaker: Toby Snyder
utterances.text: And here is an illustrative rendered view of what it could look like.

utterances.speaker: Toby Snyder
utterances.text: What we're trying to do here is break the massing down into smaller pieces, scaled at the size of many of the existing buildings in the neighborhood, and sort of take on some of that material masonry and textural quality.

utterances.speaker: Toby Snyder
utterances.text: Next slide, please.

utterances.speaker: Toby Snyder
utterances.text: This is a view from Kent Avenue and South 2nd Street.

utterances.speaker: Toby Snyder
utterances.text: This would be the southwestern corner of the project.

utterances.speaker: Toby Snyder
utterances.text: And as we noted, one of the things we can do here along Kent Avenue is pull the building back from the property line and effectively widen the sidewalk, which is something we've been carrying through

utterances.speaker: Toby Snyder
utterances.text: throughout our application and are intending to do when the project hopefully moves forward.

utterances.speaker: Toby Snyder
utterances.text: We think this is really a great way to expand the public realm, relieving congestion, creating more space for planters.

utterances.speaker: Toby Snyder
utterances.text: For sidewalk, for ground floor articulation, interaction, folks on bikes, messengers, you know, the bus route that's running along here.

utterances.speaker: Toby Snyder
utterances.text: It's just, it really deserves to be a wider street.

utterances.speaker: Toby Snyder
utterances.text: Next slide, please.

utterances.speaker: Toby Snyder
utterances.text: We're sort of articulating the building here with smaller pieces, but you can see, given the flexibility of the zoning envelope and the limited amount of FAR that can fit within that envelope, we're able to pull back at certain points here.

utterances.speaker: Toby Snyder
utterances.text: You can see we can crown the building, the rooftop with a solar canopy, with vegetation, with amenities, all of these different things that activate.

utterances.speaker: Toby Snyder
utterances.text: The building for the tenants moving in here and also really contribute to the sustainability of the project overall.

utterances.speaker: Toby Snyder
utterances.text: Next slide, please.

utterances.speaker: Toby Snyder
utterances.text: Here's another view.

utterances.speaker: Toby Snyder
utterances.text: You can see ghosted on the right-hand side is the west side of Kent Avenue, which, of course, there's construction going up right now.

utterances.speaker: Toby Snyder
utterances.text: But to the left half of the screen is our project proposed.

utterances.speaker: Toby Snyder
utterances.text: You can see, again, the massing pulled back from the street, broken down into smaller pieces, ample space to have significant...

utterances.speaker: Toby Snyder
utterances.text: Tree pits for the soil growth of the trees that could be along there.

utterances.speaker: Toby Snyder
utterances.text: So it's all about being crafted, articulated, and really a finer-grained human scale, which we think, you know, it's a

utterances.speaker: Toby Snyder
utterances.text: larger building than what is there right now, but having that human smaller fine-grained scale is a really important way to transition from the upland neighborhood into the towers across the street.

utterances.speaker: Toby Snyder
utterances.text: You can see the windows.

utterances.speaker: Toby Snyder
utterances.text: have depth, there's subtle material changes, and we sort of want to have a recall of some of the other great historic masonry buildings in the neighborhood, but executed in a contemporary way.

utterances.speaker: Toby Snyder
utterances.text: Next slide, please.

utterances.speaker: Toby Snyder
utterances.text: And finally, here's a view on South 2nd Street looking east.

utterances.speaker: Toby Snyder
utterances.text: We're actually sort of standing on a lower elevation.

utterances.speaker: Toby Snyder
utterances.text: The site does rise slope pretty significantly from Kent as you're going up to White Street.

utterances.speaker: Toby Snyder
utterances.text: The residential entrance would be off of the side streets here, not off of Kent Avenue.

utterances.speaker: Toby Snyder
utterances.text: But it is all about integrating mixed income, integrating a mix of uses, integrating a mix of scales harmoniously.

utterances.speaker: Toby Snyder
utterances.text: And now I'll turn it back to Jeremy to close.

chapters.summary: Cozen closes by noting the applicant has retained key development team members including FX Collaborative for DOB permits, New York Developers as construction manager, and other consultants, indicating intent to move forward rapidly.
chapters.title: Applicant Cozen closes with development team readiness

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: Thank you, Toby, and thank you, Chair.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: I would just like to add one last thought in closing.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: The applicant fully intends to develop the proposed development and to do so as rapidly as possible.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: To this end, the applicant has already retained key development construction team members, including expanding the scope of FX Collaborative to work on the Department of Buildings

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: permit applications, New York developers and management to be their construction manager, Muser Rutledge Consulting Engineers to be their geotechnical engineer,

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: has hired an owner's representative who will help them with code consulting, as well as Haley and Aldrich to do environmental testing.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: So the above, the retention of these...

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: Consultant

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: indicates the applicant's intent to move forward to develop this property.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: They are invested in the community.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: They are looking to build this building.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: And we look forward to hearing any questions.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: And thank you for your time.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Chair Louis asks why a portion of the project area is proposed as M1-2A manufacturing rather than mixed-use. Cozen explains three tax lots: a surface parking lot, an art storage facility, and a building with pre-existing non-conforming residential, none of which have residential development intent.
chapters.title: Chair Louis questions Cozen on M1-2A manufacturing portion

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: I have a quick question.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: I'll hand it over to Councilman Marussler.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: There's a section of the project area that would be rezoned as manufacturing M1-2A district as opposed to a mixed residential and manufacturing district.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: How was the portion determined to be proposed as manufacturing alone?

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: So there are three primary tax lots within the M12A portion.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: One is a surface parking lot that intends to remain as a parking lot.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: It is a projected development site, but it is one that we understand could be developed with community facility uses.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: The site to moving from Kent to Wythe along South 2nd, the next building is a building that was recently redeveloped, and it is an art storage facility.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: There is no intent, at least from what we've heard, to redevelop it with residential above.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: And then the last building, which is where I believe the 12 Chairs restaurant is located, and there's actually pre-existing non-conforming residential above.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: That building.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: building is going to stay as is, there's no intent to change that.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: So working with the city, it was concluded that these buildings provide, you know, there's individual reasons for each, but in totality, they have a purpose and that

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: given that this area of Williamsburg is intended to have some light manufacturing and some mix of uses, it was important to keep some of it in place.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: All right, thank you.

chapters.summary: Council Member Restler asks if the applicant has begun conversations with 32BJ for a labor agreement. Cozen confirms yes. Restler also asks about the step-down design from Kent to Wythe, and Cozen explains bulk naturally wants to be on the wider Kent Avenue side.
chapters.title: Council Member Restler questions on 32BJ agreement and step-down design

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Councilman Ressler, do you have questions?

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Chair Lewis.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: A few questions from me.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Firstly,

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: In my experience, for larger buildings like this one, it is smart to work with 32BJ.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: The workers do a great job.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: There's a great model that they have, and it's a sensible approach.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Have you begun conversations with...

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: The union, do you anticipate working out an agreement with them in advance of a vote?

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Great.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: That was the best answer.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Just one word, approval.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: I like it.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Off to a great start.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: From the first conversations I had with the development team, I don't know, two plus years ago, I've been concerned about the kind of step down that you reference in your presentation.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Similar to 325 Kent, which has the step down kind of going from Kent to our

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Board Weiss, we wanted to make sure that that same occurs here.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: And I appreciate that you've modified your proposal to reflect that.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: What assurances do we have that that will be what actually gets built?

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: So the applicant, and I can hand this over to Toby.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: So this is a rezoning.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: The buildings that we're showing you are illustrative.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: But to date, this is what the applicant has instructed their applicant team that they intend to build.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: I think there's a desire, and Toby is the architect, so I'm sure there's a lot of reasons from an architectural standpoint that he can relay.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: But from a land use planning standpoint, bulk wants to be on the wider street, not on the side streets.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: And while we are setting the building back and while there is going to be a sidewalk widening, there is a desire just from a general marketing and planning sense to have more bulk on that side.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: Toby, I'll turn it over to you if you have any specific questions.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: Reasons why the bulk wants to be on the Kent Avenue side.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Or I'll just add, is there anything that requires or forces?

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: There is nothing that technically in the zoning requires you to have it that way.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: That's it on the record.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: But from a developer's perspective, every incentive is to have the building located along close, more bulk along Kent Avenue.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: Fair enough.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: No, I mean, agreed that.

utterances.speaker: Toby Snyder
utterances.text: We're just seeking a map change, not any special bulk regulations or anything.

utterances.speaker: Toby Snyder
utterances.text: But, yeah, but to Jeremy's point, you know, there are fantastic views of the East River and the Manhattan skyline, and it makes sense to site the building in such a way to take advantage of that.

chapters.summary: Restler asks about the ownership structure. Cozen identifies the Markowitz family as the owner of Webb Holdings LLC, with no interest in the lots outside the proposed development site along South 2nd Street.
chapters.title: Council Member Restler questions on ownership structure and adjacent lots

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: As of today, who makes up the applicant team?

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: The applicant team is Web Holdings LLC.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: I think we had a slide.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: The applicant team is FX Collaborative as architect, Freed Frank as land use counsel, and AKRF as environmental.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Ownership structure is what I'm really referring to.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: Ownership structure is a...

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: LLC owned and controlled by the Markowitz family, who you have met with.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: And the relationship between the Markowitz family, the applicant team, and the lots that are outside of the proposed development?

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: The lots that are out, they have no interest in any of the lots that are located along South 2nd.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: So the parking lot, they have no ownership or control over.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: They do not own the art storage facility or the building that is, what's it called?

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: Two 12 chairs and the residential above.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: Lot 15, which is along South First Street, they are currently occupying with a, I forget the use, it's like a 3D printer.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: printing business, which is their primary business.

chapters.summary: Restler asks about neighbor concerns and whether the applicant commits to working with neighbors on quality of life issues and community investments. Cozen confirms commitment to both. Restler expresses support for the project modeled after 325 Kent.
chapters.title: Council Member Restler questions on neighbor concerns and community investment commitments

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: My office has heard from a healthy number of concerned neighbors who were worried about the impact of this development project on, I think, generally their quality of life and changing Williamsburg.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Does the applicant commit to working with neighbors and ensure

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: consistent communication and responsiveness to try to work through quality of life issues that are inevitable in a large development project like this one.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: And I think it's imperative that as our communities grow and add more housing, private applicants

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: invest in the growth of the neighborhood and ensure that the needs of the community are effectively met.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Is the applicant team committed to working with my office and the council to make that happen in advance of a vote?

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Wonderful.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: That covers it for me.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: I do just want to echo what you noted in your application.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: I think that

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: This project is kind of smartly modeled after 325 Kent, and we want to make sure that that design is incorporated, and that's why we think the density is appropriate here

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: and appreciate the, I think, consistent and clear communication from the applicant team throughout this process.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Jeremy Cozen
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.title: 289 Kent Avenue hearing closed with no public testimony

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Thank you, Councilmember.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: This panel is excused.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Thank you for being here and for your presentation.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Council, I...

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Are there any members of the public who wish to testify remotely or in person regarding this proposal?

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: No, no, he's got it.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: No, Chair, is anybody signed up online or in person regarding this project?

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: All right, this is the last call.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: If there are any members of the public who wish to testify regarding this proposal remotely, please press the raise hand button now.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: If you are in person, please identify yourself to one of the sergeant at arms.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
