chapters.summary: Chair Louis opens the hearing on pre-considered LUs for Fort Hamilton Mews, a residential rezoning in Bay Ridge, Brooklyn, Council Member Santosuosso's district. The proposal seeks ~292 apartments with ~88 permanently affordable through MIH.
chapters.title: Fort Hamilton Mews rezoning hearing opens

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: I will now stand at ease.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: I will now open the hearing on pre-considered LUs regarding Fort Hamilton Muse, a residential rezoning proposal in Bay Ridge, Brooklyn, and Councilmember Santo Soso's district.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: The applicant is seeking rezoning to a residential R7X district with a commercial overlay to develop a mixed-use residential building that would have approximately 292 apartments.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Mandatory inclusionary housing would be mapped as part of this application, which would require approximately 88 of the apartments to be permanently affordable.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: For anyone wishing to testify regarding this proposal remotely, if you have not already done so, you must register online by visiting the council's website at council.nyc.gov backslash land use.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: For anyone with us in person, please see one of the sergeants at arms to submit a speaker card.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: If you prefer to submit written testimony, you can always do so by emailing it to landyoutestimony at council.nyc.gov.

chapters.summary: Council Member Santosuosso expresses concerns about the 11-story building being one of the largest in Bay Ridge in nearly a century. She announces the Bay Ridge Triangle Community Plan, asks the applicant to withdraw until the plan is complete, and notes the applicant's refusal. She underscores the importance of a 32BJ agreement.
chapters.title: Council Member Santosuosso remarks on Bay Ridge concerns and community plan

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: I now recognize Council Member Santu Soso for remarks.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair, and good morning.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: The application before us proposes an 11-story mixed-use building in Bay Ridge, providing 292 residential units, of which 88 would be income-restricted through the Mandatory Inclusionary Housing Program.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: This would, if approved, be one of the largest buildings developed in Bay Ridge in nearly a century.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: As such, I do have concerns about this proposal, which I have made clear to the applicant.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: The applicant has been responsive in their revised design, taking into account materiality,

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: setbacks that conform with the average building height in Bay Ridge, family-sized units, rents that are more affordable, and neighborhood concerns around appropriate ground floor tenants.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: However, I do need to zoom out a little bit and talk about the context in which this application comes before us.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: Because of the charter changes that are due to take effect in January, I anticipate significant development to be proposed in this application's area.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: We refer to this area as the Triangle in Bay Ridge, specifically from 86th Street to 95th Street between 4th and 5th Avenue.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: It is primarily zoned for industrial, manufacture, and auto uses, and thus, I believe, will be a target for significant housing.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: As the charter changes,

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: Will completely remove myself and the council from the rezoning process, I am deeply concerned about allowing numerous large developments to proceed individually, site by site, without holistic planning.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: With this in mind, I strongly believe this area of my district would benefit from a comprehensive community-led planning process, as echoed by the community board and the Brooklyn Borough President.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: That is why I will be leading the Bay Ridge Triangle Community Plan, which will be launched soon.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: I have made clear to this applicant that I strongly prefer for the

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: this proposal to be considered as part of that broader neighborhood planning effort and have asked the applicant to withdraw the application until the plan is complete.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: The applicant has made clear that they are unwilling to do so and as such my chief concern with this application is that it sets the tone for a plan that my constituents have yet to weigh in on.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: I understand that the applicant may be on the verge of reaching an agreement with 32BJ today, and I would just like to underscore that it is of great importance to me that this agreement be finalized as 32BJ is an indispensable partner in this work.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: With those thoughts in mind, I look forward to discussing this application further, and I look forward to hearing the perspectives of my colleagues and constituents.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Thank you, Councilmember.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: I will now call the applicant panel for this proposal, which consists of...

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Yuri Menzak, Paul Polux, and Daniel, I'm going to let you all say your name.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Council, could you please administer the oath?

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Can you please raise your right hand and state your full name for the record?

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Oh, wait, please, you have to turn on the microphones.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Paul Prue.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Yuri Menzak.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: Daniel Grinchstein.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: And can you please raise your right?

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Do you swear to tell the truth and nothing but the truth in your testimony this morning in response to council member questions?

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: If you're all testifying, if you could keep your microphones on so you'll see a green light.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: That's how you're going to know it's on.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: There you go.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: You may now begin your testimony, which is limited to 10 minutes.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: You should start to conclude your presentation at 8 minutes.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: When you begin your presentation, please restate your name and your organization.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: You may all begin.

chapters.summary: Daniel Grinshtein presents the Fort Hamilton Mews rezoning: an R7X with C2-4 overlay, 292 units with 88 affordable at MIH Option 2 (80% AMI), 11-story building with community facility and commercial space, 75 parking spaces, on a former Staples site in Bay Ridge.
chapters.title: Applicant Grinshtein presents Fort Hamilton Mews project overview

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair Lewis.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: Good morning, Council Members.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: Thank you for having us today.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: We're here to present the Fort Hamilton Muse rezoning proposal.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: This is an R7X proposal with a C24 zoning overlay.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: So we can move to the next slide.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: And we're proposing MIH option two, which would allow for 88 of the 292 dwelling units to be income restricted at 80% average AMI.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: Our original proposal, again, is for an 11-story building with approximately 20,000 square feet of community facility space and 30,000 square feet of commercial space on a gross square footage basis.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: What you see up there are the zoning square footages.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: We would include 75 parking spaces, most of which are voluntary, in a sub-cellar below grade, and initially the commercial space was proposed to be a grocery store.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: Next slide.

chapters.summary: Grinshtein shows the site location in Bay Ridge, the surrounding C8 automotive district and multifamily housing, and the proposed R7X zoning line drawn at the center of the block between R5B and R6B districts.
chapters.title: Applicant Grinshtein on Bay Ridge site context and zoning

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: This shows where the project is in Bay Ridge, Brooklyn.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: Next slide.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: This is an old Staples site.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: As you know, there was a period of time when big box retail was in abundance around the city, and it's to some degree being redeveloped now.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: Staples has changed their business model, and we have a long-term, or we own the property, and we have a few more years left on the lease.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: And a right to terminate the lease, we're going to do so as soon as we're ready to construct and build the proposed building in this location.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: There you see the triangle between Fifth Avenue and Fourth Avenue as the avenues start and extend north through the borough of Brooklyn.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: Next slide.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: Close up of the site.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: Next slide.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: This shows the uses the council member referred to immediately across the street from us, the C8 district with primarily automotive uses.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: And then in the areas surrounding the commercial core, there is predominantly multifamily housing.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: Which is approximately six stories in most locations, or no greater than six stories.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: Next slide.

chapters.summary: Grinshtein describes the proposed rezoning details: R7X with 145-foot height limit, 6.0 FAR for residential, MIH designation, and the building's three distinct materialities designed to break up the 300-foot frontage.
chapters.title: Applicant Grinshtein on R7X zoning details and building design

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: Again, the proposed rezoning in the Bay Ridge Special District.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: This is a mix of R5B and R6B along the avenue.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: We would draw the R7X line in the center of the block.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: Next slide.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: There you see the entry to the approximately 50 parking space surface parking lot in front of the stables, which would be redeveloped.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: Next slide.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: Some more views of the site with the Verrazano Bridge in the background.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: Next slide.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: The largely traditional retail strip to our south, the proposed development would draw that together with the commercial district to the north.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: Next slide.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: And fill what is essentially a gap with ground floor active retail uses.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: With an entrance at the corner underneath the white section of the building and then the community facility entrance on the in the red section of the building.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: Here you see the building with three sort of distinct materialities, a white more modern box divided

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: by glass with a more traditional red brick box to the north.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: It's a 300-foot site, so it's quite an expanse.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: And the idea here was to break up the building with different parts to provide some diversity of appearance and materials.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: Next slide.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: So this would require a zoning text amendment to add the MIH designation and would change the zoning map.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: Next slide.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: There you see the two zoning districts compared.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: Next slide.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: So R7X would have 125 foot, or sorry, 145 foot height limit, 6.0 FAR for residential uses.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: Various FAR limits for commercial and community facility uses.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: Next slide.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: We're going to come back to that slide shortly.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: There you see the mapped MIH designated area.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: Next slide.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: So in summary, this proposal located immediately across the street from the terminus of the N train would be a good place for density.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: It's got a wide avenue immediately.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: It sits on a wide avenue.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: It bridges, you know, it's...

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: The triangle sort of bridges the gap between two avenues, and then we have the Fort Hamilton Triangle Park to our southwest.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: So this is an expanse of open space that would provide views and contrast with the taller building.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: Located on the corner.

chapters.summary: Grinshtein addresses Community Board 10's recommendation to disapprove and their R6A suggestion. He presents an alternative R7D designation reducing height to 125 feet and FAR to 5.6, with a redesigned building as a compromise to avoid appeals or refiling under the new charter changes.
chapters.title: Applicant Grinshtein presents R7D alternative in response to community board

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: So as you know, we attended community board meetings and hearings and had a lot of very interesting feedback on our proposal.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: And I think that the conclusion was that the community board recommended an R6A in the context of the planning that you're proposing to do now.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: And while we have no interest in withdrawing our application for R7X, we heard the remarks of the community and the feedback that we received and

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: have spent the last couple of months working on something that might bridge the gap between what they're proposing and what we proposed.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: So we have some.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: ideas about how that might look and what that might look like in an effort to allow the project to move forward without having to go to

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: an appeals board or refile under the new regime starting in January.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: We have looked at

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: very closely what an R7D designation, how that would affect the site.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: Next slide.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: So next slide.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: An R7D, here you have the very small details of what R7X looks like, but really it's the summary of the height and the FAR.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: Next slide.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: And so if you take the R7X that we showed here earlier, and then you add the R7D to the right, you'll see that it brings the total height

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: of the building down to 125 and the FAR to 5.6, most importantly.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: And so that would be a small but meaningful, from our side, reduction in the proposed building.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: But I think more importantly, we took the moment or we took the opportunity to redesign the building with some different materiality and different arrangement of heights and setbacks.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: Next slide.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: Next slide.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: That was R7D there, which you can look at at greater length in the recorded material.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: Here is the proposed redesign.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: We've taken a, and maybe it's better to turn this over to Yuri to talk about the new materiality and the massing.

chapters.summary: Yuri Menzak presents the redesigned building: a six-story street wall with two building masses above, 30-foot setback from the northern lot line, 60-foot courtyard between buildings, and contextual materiality to reduce the perception of a 300-foot-long building.
chapters.title: Architect Menzak presents revised Fort Hamilton Mews design and massing

utterances.speaker: Yuri Menzak
utterances.text: Yeah, if we could go to the next slide, please.

utterances.speaker: Yuri Menzak
utterances.text: Okay, so the number of comments that we have received from the neighborhood refer to the scale of it and the fact that the 9 and 11 story setbacks that would begin

utterances.speaker: Yuri Menzak
utterances.text: would not fit within the neighborhood.

utterances.speaker: Yuri Menzak
utterances.text: And as a result, we have tried to replicate a six-story line with our parapet and a setback on majority of the building and created a two-building type of setup above the six-story.

utterances.speaker: Yuri Menzak
utterances.text: So the articulation of the street wall is within the five to eight feet for the 300 feet section of the frontage on the Fifth Avenue.

utterances.speaker: Yuri Menzak
utterances.text: But above that, we basically have two buildings.

utterances.speaker: Yuri Menzak
utterances.text: One on the left, which is a smaller version that provides the light and air to the northern portion of the building, providing a setback of 30 feet from the northern lot line.

utterances.speaker: Yuri Menzak
utterances.text: And also providing a 60 feet court in between the buildings as well.

utterances.speaker: Yuri Menzak
utterances.text: That articulation, I think, is...

utterances.speaker: Yuri Menzak
utterances.text: up in terms of the presence of 300 feet long and 11 story building presence on the avenue and have made it in our opinion a bit pleasant more pleasant

utterances.speaker: Yuri Menzak
utterances.text: perception of the mass and the volumes also we

utterances.speaker: Yuri Menzak
utterances.text: Introduced number of setbacks above the minimum base height of 60 feet.

utterances.speaker: Yuri Menzak
utterances.text: In R7G, 60 feet is the minimum required street wall height.

utterances.speaker: Yuri Menzak
utterances.text: And above that, we went up to the 95 feet, and we stepped back the rest of the building in order to comply with the 15 and 10 feet required setbacks from the street lines.

chapters.summary: Chair Louis asks how the applicant is addressing Community Board 10's concerns. Grinshtein explains the revised design with contextual setbacks at six stories, two distinct masses, and historic materials responding to architectural concerns.
chapters.title: Chair Louis questions Grinshtein on Community Board 10 concerns

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: I have a couple of questions, and I'll hand it over to Councilmember Sato Soso.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: How are you addressing Community Board 10's concerns given the recommendation to disapprove this proposal?

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: Well, what you see here is a building that speaks to the architectural sort of comments and concerns.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: And so we pivoted in providing something that we believe is more contextual to the neighborhood and that fits better while maintaining the same basic mass, albeit a small reduction from the 6.0.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: It's an 11-story building, and it sets back at six stories, which is essentially the community context.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: And it breaks it apart into two masses that...

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: that are allowed, the rearrangement allows us to have the height at the corner where it's most appropriate and then, you know, a very large sort of reduction in the center of the site at six stories

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: with another massing.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: So it, instead of looking like a very large

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: 300-foot-long building.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: It looks like two different buildings, and again, with a more historic context.

chapters.summary: Chair Louis asks about commercial tenant plans. Grinshtein says initial grocery store conversations shifted to smaller service retail after community feedback, though social media indicated desire for Trader Joe's or Aldi.
chapters.title: Chair Louis questions Grinshtein on commercial tenant plans

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: What types of commercial tenants will you be seeking for the proposed commercial space, and have you begun any discussions with prospective tenants?

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: We haven't had any conversations with prospective tenants.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: Beyond the initial conversations with grocery store operators.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: We did hear, though, from the community that perhaps smaller retail spaces would be more desirable than the large single operator, which was a bit of a surprise on account of the fact that a lot of social media

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: indicates that Trader Joe's or Aldi would have been desirable here.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: So we've redesigned, we intend to occupy the ground floor spaces with more traditional service retail.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Council Member Santosuosso asks the applicant to confirm they are proceeding without withdrawing despite the community plan. She clarifies the revised R7D building height is 115 feet (below the 125-foot maximum) and the grocery store is no longer the primary ground floor goal.
chapters.title: Council Member Santosuosso questions on withdrawal, R7D height, and grocery store

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: I will now call on Council Member Santos also for questions.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: So I just want to just briefly clarify that you all are aware that we're launching a neighborhood planning process and it continues to be that you're continuing forward with the application and not withdrawing.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: In absence of withdrawing your application, will you agree to be part of the plan post-entitlement, should you receive it, to ensure your building conforms with community's calls for contextual design and other elements?

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: I just want to clarify.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: So you initially proposed in your first proposal, you proposed a building of 145 feet.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: You are now in this revised R7D in response to the community's concerns.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: You've brought that down.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: And even though an R7D allows for 125 feet, the building you're proposing now is?

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: 115 feet.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: And you just said that in response to the community's concerns about traffic and congestion, you're no longer moving forward with the grocery store as the primary goal moving forward on the ground floor.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: Can you speak about your efforts to reach an agreement with 32BJ?

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: Yeah, I think that.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: It was a little slow in starting, but we've engaged them with a very productive dialogue in the last days.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: And I believe that as we're arriving here this morning, we have indication that we have an agreement.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: For a neutrality agreement, a traditional neutrality agreement, and that we intend to, you know, we were going to do prevailing wage anyways.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: So the idea of working with the union in this case seems like it's a reasonable request.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: So it is your intent to reach an agreement with 32B for the building.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: Okay.

chapters.summary: Santosuosso asks about 32BJ negotiations. Grinshtein reports a neutrality agreement has been reached with 32BJ, with prevailing wage commitment. Santosuosso then asks about appeals board use if the council rejects the application.
chapters.title: Council Member Santosuosso questions on 32BJ agreement and appeals board

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: Something you mentioned earlier is that you were looking into the legal tools available to you should the council not support this rezoning application.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: So does that mean that if the council does not support the rezoning application that you would seek use of the appeals board, for instance?

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: For instance, yes.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: And the appeals board is largely untested, but in the event that we received a negative

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: reaction there, our second opportunity to get the project approved would be to file in January the same application.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: And to pursue an approval through ULURP under the new abbreviated timeframe.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: And, of course, that would bypass me and the council completely.

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: And in that case, would you be proposing a building at R7X or at R7D?

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: It seems to me that you're now coming to the council and saying you're proposing it at an R7D.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: If you were to use these new tools, are you coming back with an R7X?

utterances.speaker: Daniel Grinchstein
utterances.text: We would most certainly come back with an R7X or perhaps even a greater R8 or R9 Sony designation.

chapters.summary: Grinshtein confirms that if rejected, the applicant could use the appeals board or refile in January under the new abbreviated ULURP timeline, bypassing the council entirely. Santosuosso asks if they would return with R7X; Grinshtein confirms they would come back with R7X or potentially R8/R9.
chapters.title: Council Member Santosuosso questions on refiling at higher density if rejected

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: Just with the remainder of my time, and this is not a problem that you alone as developers can solve, but it's imperative in this moment that we're in where the prevailing belief is that our only way out of the housing crisis is to build, build, build,

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: that it is actually important to have actual affordable housing that is not inflationary to local rent costs and that actually fits in with the neighborhood character.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: I need to express on the record my frustration that even though we will be able to vote on the rezoning application in front of us, that because the applicant is not withdrawing and will come back in January should we vote it down, that our hands are somewhat tied here.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: And that's a frustrating reality for my constituents.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: But I am appreciative that you have been responsive to our concerns, and I look forward to continuing the conversation.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Thank you, Council Member.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: This panel is now excused.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Council, are there any members of the public who wish to testify remotely or in person regarding this proposal?

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Yes, we have one member in person and one member online.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: We will start with the one member in person.

chapters.summary: Santosuosso expresses frustration on the record that the council's hands are tied because the applicant can return in January under new charter changes, bypassing community input. She appreciates the applicant's responsiveness but notes the difficult reality for constituents.
chapters.title: Council Member Santosuosso expresses frustration with tied council hands under new charter

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: We now call on Kyron Banks from 32BJ.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Penningberg
utterances.text: I'm not Karan, but I'm here with 32BJ.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Penningberg
utterances.text: He's going to testify on the FIPS proposal.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Penningberg
utterances.text: Right.

chapters.summary: Veronica Urovosky, a Brooklyn resident, strongly supports the project, noting it would provide almost 90 affordable homes in Bay Ridge where only 5 affordable units were built in 12 years. She criticizes representatives using procedural excuses to delay housing.
chapters.title: Public testimony: Veronica Urovosky supports Fort Hamilton Mews

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis

utterances.speaker: Council Staff

utterances.text: Yes, my name is Veronica and I live in Brooklyn.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Veronica Urovosky
utterances.text: I'm here today because like the majority of renters in the city, including many people I personally know and love, I'm paying too much for housing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Veronica Urovosky
utterances.text: So needless to say, I'm very much in favor of this project.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Veronica Urovosky

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Veronica Urovosky

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Veronica Urovosky

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Veronica Urovosky
utterances.text: That's almost 90 units more than the affordable units the current staples in a parking lot provide.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Veronica Urovosky

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Veronica Urovosky

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Veronica Urovosky

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Veronica Urovosky

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Veronica Urovosky

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Veronica Urovosky

utterances.text: Building this project would make housing prices worse.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Veronica Urovosky
utterances.text: So I hope this project is approved now and not later.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Veronica Urovosky
utterances.text: And I hope that it helps alleviate this crunch even a tiny bit.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Veronica Urovosky
utterances.text: Thank you for your time.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis

chapters.summary: Richard Lobel of Sheldon Lobel PC presents the 21-31 46th Avenue rezoning for applicant Ashley Fina, seeking to rezone from M1-4/R6B to R7X with C2-5 overlay. The 11-story building would have ~84 units with 15 affordable at MIH Option 1, on a transit-rich site with no residential displacement.
chapters.title: Applicant Lobel presents 21-31 46th Avenue project overview

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair Lewis, Councilmember Juan, Committee Council, Richard Lobel of Sheldon Lobel, joined by Ashley Fina, who is our applicant, Nick Labaris, the project architect, Christina Zapansky from GZA Environmental.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: We're here today to discuss, as Councilmember Juan suggested, the 2131-46th Avenue rezoning.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: The next slide is a summary in terms of what the rezoning accomplishes.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: We've got an existing M14R6B zoning district.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: That district has been set since 2004.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: And despite the R6B designation, in the last 25 years, there's been no housing produced on the site.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: In fact, we have an underbuilt commercial building with 15 parking spaces.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: The proposal would allow for a rezoning to an R7XC25 district to produce a new 11-story, roughly 81,000 square foot community facility, commercial, and residential building.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: with roughly 84 units.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: This is important to us because we've got an existing property here, which is central to transportation, as we'll talk about in the slides to come, with no residential displacement.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: in an area where there is already some infrastructure to accommodate a building of this nature.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: In addition to the rezoning, we of course would be asking for a mandatory inclusionary housing text amendment.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: In the current iteration, this would result in roughly 21 permanently affordable homes.

chapters.summary: Lobel details the building: 11 stories, 81,000 sq ft, 84 units with 52 two-to-three bedroom units (two-thirds), 15 affordable units proportional in bedroom count, and 15 voluntary parking spaces reduced from initial design after Community Board 2 feedback.
chapters.title: Applicant Lobel on building details and family-sized units

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: The next slide.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: The numbers behind the proposed development, again, an 11-story building.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: This mirrors the condo building immediately to the east of the site.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: Floor area of 81,000 square feet, base height of 67 feet, and a total height of 120 feet.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: The number of units here we're particularly proud of, particularly in light of the fact that 52 out of these 84 units, roughly two-thirds, are at two to three bedrooms.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: Importantly, as per the MIH program, the affordable units in the building will reflect those two to three bedrooms as well.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: They will be roughly proportional to the units generally in the building.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: So we're creating some really nice sized units for some members of the community who will be seeking affordable housing.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: In addition to that, while there is no parking required, we did provide 15 voluntary spaces in the cellar.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: This is something which was reduced from the first iteration after the discussion with Community Board 2.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: Nick can talk about that when he talks about the illustrative building.

chapters.summary: Lobel shows the zoning map, noting the site is immediately adjacent to an existing R7X district with 11-17 and 48-story buildings nearby. He explains the approach of extending the existing R7X district to cover the property, a favored approach by City Planning.
chapters.title: Applicant Lobel on zoning map and adjacent R7X context

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: The next slide is the zoning map.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: Kind of chunky and difficult to see, but you can see that the site currently is zoned M14R6B, but is immediately adjacent to an R7X district.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: Indeed, across the street in the R73 district, the area is produced.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: many large buildings, buildings at 11 stories, 17 stories, and 48 stories.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: So while we are only 150 to 200 feet from these sites, we are definitely within the area and shadow of many of these extremely tall buildings.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: And so our building would allow for moderate density to the west of those large sites.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: The next slide is the tax map, which shows the extent of the zoning district boundary.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: Here, as per discussions with city planning, we're taking an existing R7X with a commercial overlay and dragging it to encompass the property of the west.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: This is a favored course of rezoning by city planning, which allows for contextual zoning to take an existing zoning district and to move it to cover the building.

chapters.summary: Lobel presents the area map showing proximity to subway entrances, Murray Playground, and the wide Jackson Avenue. He notes City Planning recognized the opportunity to add housing with no residential displacement on a transit-oriented site.
chapters.title: Applicant Lobel on area context, transit, and site advantages

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: The next slide is the area map, which has, I think, some great rationale in terms of why we think the rezoning is appropriate.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: As was noted, in every agency and board we spoke to, we are nearly adjacent to subway entrances.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: It is indeed a transit-rich area, which allows for several subway stops within blocks of the property, in addition to which, of course, Murray Playground exists within a block of the property.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: We have a 48-story building, again, in front of the property.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: And the intersection of 46th Avenue and Jackson Avenue here, a wide street, allows for somewhat of a wider expanse in front of this building.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: So all these things taken together allow for a nice amount of space in front of the building, a street system, and a transportation system, which lend themselves to a rezoning of this nature, in addition to which, as was noted by City-Council,

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: planning, the opportunity to add housing on a site where you would result in no residential displacement and really allow for people to take advantage of transit and such in the area was a rare opportunity.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: The next slide is an eagle-eye view of the area.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: One notes the tall buildings in the immediate area, again, ranging from 11 to 48 stories.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: This is no secret to anyone who's familiar with the area.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: And the next several slides show pictures of the site as well as the surrounding area.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: We note the existing TD Bank underbuilt for the site and parking immediately adjacent, really not serving much in terms of community needs.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: I would pass the microphone over to Nick Labaris, who can discuss the illustrated plans and materials, and then we're happy to answer questions.

utterances.speaker: Nick Labaris
utterances.text: We have something that we think is a great site to make a pleasant backdrop to the plaza.

utterances.speaker: Nick Labaris
utterances.text: And we don't think that there's anything that's going to be...

utterances.speaker: Nick Labaris
utterances.text: let's say, like, deleterious to this block, other than the fact that there will be some sort of building being built, you know.

utterances.text: So you'll have the normal stuff that you have to deal with.

utterances.speaker: Christina Zapansky

chapters.summary: Won asks about community engagement and how concerns will be incorporated. Lobel discusses MIH requirements, family-sized affordable units, architectural mitigation, greenery contributions, and art space commitments. Labaris explains the massing decisions to keep the building at 11 stories as a sensitive compromise.
chapters.title: Council Member Won questions on community engagement and affordability

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: Thank you so much for your presentation.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: Throughout the public review process, residents of the surrounding area of this project have expressed deep concerns related to affordability, community benefits, street-level design, and greenery and building size.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: What have you done to engage the members of the surrounding neighborhood, and how will you incorporate the community priorities into the project?

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: Yeah, so thank you, Councilmember Wan.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: And, you know, we've had some very productive conversations with some of our surrounding neighbors.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: And, you know, one of the things that they mentioned was that they're not opposed to new development.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: I think an important distinction here between the R7X to the east of us and us is that we're providing mandatory inclusionary housing.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: So, of course, since 2016, this is a requirement.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: We're happy to do it.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: And really what it is is it allows us to cross-subsidize through no city subsidy to allow for the creation of these affordable units.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: In our case, an average unit size for these affordable units of over two bedrooms, so two to three bedrooms.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: So there were things I think that we can do and things that I think have been a challenge for us.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: The things that we can do, and Nick, who's an experienced applicant in terms of an architect and has built buildings across the city, we've talked a lot about architectural aspects of the building.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: what we can do to try to mitigate some of the height effects, and the opportunity to create some greenery around the space.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: I know that there's a pedestrian triangle to the front of the building.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: We've talked to the area about perhaps donating or trying to contribute to allowing for more greenery in that space as well.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: Ms.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: Leong, who is one of the attendees of the conversation we had with community members, discussed an opportunity to commit to certain land use trusts in the area.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: And Ashley has said that she'd be more than willing to do that.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: Ashley has, since the beginning, has told me in no uncertain terms that she'd like to try to give as much as possible, particularly in terms of art space and the opportunity for artists,

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: given the nature of the surrounding area, as well as the opportunity to greenify the area and provide some assistance to parklands in the area.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: I know that Murray Playground is a heavily utilized playground in the area.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: And while city planning noted that as being a positive of rezoning here, the truth is that playgrounds need resources and they can benefit from local contributions.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: So with that in mind, we're thrilled to be able to do that.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: I think that in terms of the building itself, we did make changes, as we discussed, to the parking as well as to the curb cuts.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: The massing of the building, I think, has been a little bit more of a challenge.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: I know that Nick did some research into the adjacent building.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: It is somewhat at an angle to the building, so it's not immediately abutting.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: And the opportunity we had to mass some of the bulk away from the sides.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: has basically put us to the 11-story height of the building.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: So, Nick, I don't know if you just want to address that briefly.

utterances.speaker: Nick Labaris
utterances.text: Yeah, sure.

utterances.speaker: Nick Labaris
utterances.text: I mean, we could reduce the height of the building.

utterances.speaker: Nick Labaris
utterances.text: We could reduce the height of the building by going much, I think, much, much deeper to the backyard because right now you can go and have up to a height of 75 feet, about 20 feet for the backyard.

utterances.speaker: Nick Labaris
utterances.text: So we can basically fatten up the building, and we could go back to the sides and go back to 10 floors.

utterances.speaker: Nick Labaris
utterances.text: But it just seems like the more sensitive thing to do would just be to be nice to these neighbors because, I mean, ultimately these are the people that are the ones who are actually opposing it.

utterances.speaker: Nick Labaris
utterances.text: It's people that are in this condo and also the people that are on the backside of the block that don't want to have to deal with a construction site.

utterances.speaker: Nick Labaris
utterances.text: So, you know, trying to be mindful of them, we think that this is a good solution.

utterances.speaker: Nick Labaris
utterances.text: And it's also better urbanistically, too, we think, just because it's a much better backdrop for the plaza.

utterances.speaker: Nick Labaris
utterances.text: So all things considered, you know, this seems to be like a really reasonable compromise.

utterances.speaker: Nick Labaris
utterances.text: And it's, you know, well within the character of all this other surrounding fabric in this one spot, you know.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: And so the opportunity here, particularly in light of the nature of this district, we'd be happy to engage in that conversation and to give everyone a say.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: in terms of what that space is used for.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: Right now, as we're looking at building more family-sized units, there's not enough school seats.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: Are you looking to make sure that there's an early childhood care provider who's going to be on the ground floor space?

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: We haven't.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: I think it's something we'd be happy to look at.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: Part of our diligence in terms of environmental review is to look at school seats.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: I know, Christina, that we've looked at that as part of the environmental review.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: For 3K and pre-K and twos and zeros.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: I'm not talking about grade school.

utterances.speaker: Christina Zapansky
utterances.text: For that, I only have for PS and IS.

utterances.speaker: Julie Won
utterances.text: Yeah, she didn't look at early childhood education.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: So to the extent that that space would be a valuable contribution in terms of the opportunity to get younger kids in for school seats, we'd be happy to look at that.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: And just, again, Ashley's been a great applicant.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: The application has been outstanding for some time, but we're happy to engage in that conversation to try to give back in that regard.

chapters.summary: Olivia Wang opposes the rezoning, arguing the public review process was flawed because advisory bodies voted on a 70-unit project before the revised 84-unit EAS was released. She cites severe open space deficit (0.094 acres per 1,000 residents), unnecessary cellar parking in a flood zone, and urges rejection of R7X in favor of a four-story contextual building.
chapters.title: Public testimony: Olivia Wang opposes rezoning, cites flawed review and open space deficit

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Olivia Wang
utterances.text: Good afternoon, my name is Olivia Wang.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Olivia Wang
utterances.text: I'm here to speak against the rezoning of 213146th Avenue.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Olivia Wang
utterances.text: First, the public review process for this project was fundamentally flawed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Olivia Wang
utterances.text: Community Board 2 and Queensborough President issued recommendation based on an outdated 70-unit project description.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Olivia Wang
utterances.text: Only after those advisory bodies voted did the applicant release a revised EAS for an 84-unit project with reduced parking.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Olivia Wang
utterances.text: Advisory approvals granted on an incomplete record should not stand.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Olivia Wang
utterances.text: The paperwork changed, but the core issue still did not.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Olivia Wang
utterances.text: The applicant is still seeking a massive R7X entitlement, allowing heights up to 145 feet, right next to low-rise residential context.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Olivia Wang
utterances.text: We're talking three, four floors tall.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Olivia Wang
utterances.text: Second, the revised review confirms serious unmitigated impacts.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Olivia Wang
utterances.text: There's severe open space deficit in this area.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Olivia Wang
utterances.text: The surrounding area has an open space ratio of just 0.094 acres per 1,000 residents, drastically lower than the city's 2.5 acres.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Olivia Wang
utterances.text: Adding over 200 residents without providing any public open space will only worsen an already critical shortage.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Olivia Wang
utterances.text: The project includes unnecessary cellular parking space, even after community boards to conditional approval included eliminating the cellular parking.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Olivia Wang
utterances.text: In a flood zone, excavating 135,000 cubic feet of earth creates unnecessary flooding risks in an area that already experiences flooding.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Olivia Wang
utterances.text: Curb cuts impact and severe structural hazards for adjacent occupied buildings.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Olivia Wang
utterances.text: Lastly, when I see finally establish a baseline for what our community truly deserves.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Olivia Wang
utterances.text: This install of a project offers absolutely nothing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Olivia Wang
utterances.text: Council member one, are you ready to let our community's hard-won progress

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Olivia Wang
utterances.text: risk to be utterly ignored and just thrown into the trash.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Olivia Wang
utterances.text: I respectfully urge the council to reject the R7X entitlement and cap any redevelopment at a low-rise four-story

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Olivia Wang
utterances.text: contextual building, eliminating all voluntary cellular parking to reduce excavation and flood risks, and enforce the precedent set by 1LIC.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Olivia Wang
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Now we have Ansel.

utterances.speaker: Tahir Demirjolo
utterances.text: If you can go next slide.

utterances.speaker: Tahir Demirjolo
utterances.text: You can see this in the greater context of massing if it's well within the urban context.

utterances.speaker: Tahir Demirjolo
utterances.text: Next one, please.

utterances.speaker: Tahir Demirjolo
utterances.text: One more.

utterances.speaker: Tahir Demirjolo
utterances.text: One more.

utterances.text: This is the proximity of the subway station.

utterances.speaker: Tahir Demirjolo
utterances.text: On the ground floor, we have a commercial or community facility building, sorry, commercial use facing 108th Street.

utterances.speaker: Tahir Demirjolo
utterances.text: Residential entrance is along the narrow street.

utterances.speaker: Tahir Demirjolo
utterances.text: There are no cellar space here, so the ground floor houses the lobby and the mechanical spaces.

utterances.speaker: Tahir Demirjolo

utterances.speaker: Tahir Demirjolo
utterances.text: On the typical floor plan, as you can see, there's a central core, which is actually exposed to the street, creating daylight into the corridors and improving the quality of life for the residents.

utterances.speaker: Tahir Demirjolo
utterances.text: I think that will be it in a nutshell.

chapters.summary: Lobel summarizes the application: no residential displacement, good street access, near mass transportation, and strong community board consensus (36-4). He notes productive conversations with CB6 and willingness to engage on programming commercial space.
chapters.title: Applicant Lobel summarizes 69-67 108th Street application

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: So just to conclude.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: This site here, again, is a site where no residential displacement would occur.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: We have a street system where there's good access to the site.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: We are near mass transportation.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: And I think that's why many people in the community found this to be a potentially beneficial site in terms of creating housing here.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: We did have some very...

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: productive conversations with the community board, which were, you know, we built on those conversations.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: They were lengthy and good.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: And I think that, you know, we did end up with a really strong consensus from them that this was something that would be desired by the area.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: So with that, the Alpec team is happy to answer any questions.

chapters.summary: Chair Louis asks about the green space width behind the one-story home (15 feet, per Demirjolo) and where loading deliveries and trash pickup will be located (residential on 17th Avenue, commercial on 108th Street).
chapters.title: Chair Louis questions on green space and loading/trash location

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Thank you for your presentation.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: I have a few quick questions before I hand it over to Councilman Shulman.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Directly behind the proposed development site is a one-story home.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: I wanted to know how wide would the proposed green space be?

utterances.speaker: Tahir Demirjolo
utterances.text: 15 feet.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: 15 feet, okay.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: And Chair Lewis, just to note that that owner did appear at the hearing and express that to the applicant that he was in favor of the application.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Okay, thank you for sharing that.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Where will loading deliveries and trash pickup be located on the site?

utterances.speaker: Tahir Demirjolo
utterances.text: For residential, we're planning to be along the 17th Avenue.

utterances.speaker: Tahir Demirjolo
utterances.text: And for the commercial, it will be along 108th Street.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Okay.

chapters.summary: Council Member Schulman asks about deeper affordability. Lobel says the project margins don't lend themselves to 30% AMI but is happy to discuss further. Schulman asks which MIH option; Lobel says Option 1 and Option 2 have been penciled, applicant accepts Option 1.
chapters.title: Council Member Schulman questions on affordability and MIH option

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Council Member Shulman?

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Yeah, thank you.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Would you be willing to commit to deeper affordability than the minimum required under MIH?

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: Yeah, you know, we've talked about this as an applicant team.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: I think one of the benefits of this project is that we're able to keep the unit sizes somewhat large.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: And of course, because of MIH and the regulations therein, those units will be, the larger units will be available to the affordable units in the same ratio as they are in the building.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: I'd say that while we do regularly have projects where we are able to provide increased affordability, including, for example, 30% in option one, I don't think that the margins in this application would really lend themselves to that.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: It is a relatively small project in terms of the numbers, only 59 units.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: So I'm happy to talk to Gabby about that in the future.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: But at this point, I think it would be somewhat challenging.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Which MIH option are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: We have penciled out.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: Option one and option two, but the applicant understands and is accepting of option one to the extent that's selected by the council.

chapters.summary: Schulman asks about ground floor tenant types. Lobel says the community board expressed interest in grocery, cafe, or community/medical space, and the applicant is open to discussion. Schulman asks about setbacks and facade materials; Lobel confirms facade changes incorporated but setbacks more challenging.
chapters.title: Council Member Schulman questions on ground floor tenants and facade materials

utterances.text: Do you have any type of particular type of tenant in mind for the ground floor?

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: I know you mentioned that.

utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.text: The community board made some recommendations regarding setbacks and facade materials.

utterances.text: Are you able to incorporate those?

utterances.text: We are able to incorporate the facade material suggestions and have done so on the most recent rendering.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: I think that the setbacks have been somewhat more challenging.

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: Tahir, do you want to talk about that for a minute?

utterances.speaker: Tahir Demirjolo
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Tahir Demirjolo
utterances.text: We wanted to keep the building height lower to...

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Understood.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Okay.

chapters.summary: Schulman asks about funding improvements to McDonald Park. Lobel confirms willingness. Schulman raises stormwater concerns, noting the area floods increasingly and concrete front yards contribute to 108th Street flooding. She asks the applicant to be mindful.
chapters.title: Council Member Schulman questions on McDonald Park funding and stormwater

utterances.text: The borough president recommended the project fund improvements to McDonald Park, which is nearby.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Is that something the applicant would consider?

utterances.speaker: Richard Lobel
utterances.text: We would definitely consider that.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: And I know you mentioned about the stormwater and all of that, which I appreciate.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: You know, just so you know, that area has more and more become flooded when we have these rainstorms.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: So...

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: That's an issue.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: And the more development we have, you know, all over the place, not just there, but...

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: It's a problem.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: And the, so in that area, it was rezoned and there was a lot of legislation way long time ago, but a lot of the homes that are there have concrete in front of them and not green.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: So that contributes to 108th Street getting flooded.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: So I want you just to be mindful of that.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: That's all the questions I have right at the moment.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: I have others I'll let you know.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Thank you, Council Member.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: This panel is now excused.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Chair Louis opens the hearing on pre-considered LUs for Sojourner Truth MAPES, a mixed-use residential rezoning in the Crotona neighborhood of the Bronx, Council Member Feliz's district. The proposal seeks 457 apartments with 137 permanently affordable through MIH.

chapters.summary: Matthew Washington of Phipps Houses introduces the team and provides background on Phipps Houses, a nonprofit founded in 1905 with 10,000 affordable apartments. He notes Phipps has served the Crotona Park West Farms community for over 50 years and that the project will relocate MAPES Court tenants to new homes.
chapters.title: Applicant Washington introduces Phipps Houses and Sojourner Truth MAPES project

utterances.speaker: Matthew Washington
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Matthew Washington
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair Lewis and Council, for your endurance.

utterances.speaker: Matthew Washington
utterances.text: It's been a full day.

utterances.speaker: Matthew Washington
utterances.text: We're glad to be here.

utterances.speaker: Matthew Washington
utterances.text: My name is Matthew Washington, Vice President and Chief of Staff at Phipps Houses.

utterances.speaker: Matthew Washington
utterances.text: We're excited to talk with you about a 100% affordable housing project built across two new buildings.

utterances.speaker: Matthew Washington
utterances.text: I just want to make mention of my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: Matthew Washington
utterances.text: I'm joined with Kelly Biscuso, Vice President of Development at Phipps Houses, Astrid Walker-Stewart, Director of Planning and Real Estate Development at Phipps Houses, and we're also joined by our architect, Magnus Westergren, who's an associate at Marvel Architects, and our...

utterances.speaker: Matthew Washington
utterances.text: environmental consultant Patrick Blanchfield, who's senior vice president at AKRF.

utterances.speaker: Matthew Washington
utterances.text: So we'll talk a little bit about the project and then we'll go into it.

utterances.speaker: Matthew Washington
utterances.text: Next slide, please.

utterances.speaker: Matthew Washington
utterances.text: Just a little background on who we are at FIPS.

utterances.speaker: Matthew Washington
utterances.text: So FIPS Houses is a nonprofit organization that's been around since 1905.

utterances.speaker: Matthew Washington
utterances.text: So 121 years of building and providing affordable housing here in New York City.

utterances.speaker: Matthew Washington
utterances.text: Today we have about 10,000 apartments, 100% affordable across New York City.

utterances.speaker: Matthew Washington
utterances.text: We also recognize the need for supports beyond that.

utterances.speaker: Matthew Washington
utterances.text: And so in 1972, established a nonprofit organization, FIPS Neighborhoods, which provides social service supports for members of our buildings, but also the communities we serve, building community centers and the like.

utterances.speaker: Matthew Washington
utterances.text: Welcome, Councilmember Felice.

utterances.speaker: Matthew Washington
utterances.text: We have been doing this work for many years, and we have been serving this community, the Cortona Park West Farms neighborhood, for over 50 years, and we're very proud of that.

utterances.speaker: Matthew Washington
utterances.text: With this project, we're excited because the building that we're going to talk about at Mabe's Court, originally built in the 1920s, we got renovated it in 1991.

utterances.speaker: Matthew Washington
utterances.text: It's a walk-up building, and so through this project, we'll be able to give our existing tenants brand new homes in a brand new building and pay for relocation across the street and keep them in the same neighborhood.

utterances.speaker: Matthew Washington
utterances.text: So excited for that and to create more affordable housing in the neighborhood.

utterances.speaker: Matthew Washington
utterances.text: And I'm going to pass the virtual mic over to my colleague, Astrid.

utterances.speaker: Matthew Washington
utterances.text: who will walk through more details of the project.

utterances.speaker: Matthew Washington
utterances.text: Next slide, please.

chapters.summary: Astrid Walker-Stewart presents the two zoning map amendments and text amendment: rezoning the Sojourner site from R7-1 to R8, and the MAPES Court site from R7-1/C1-4 to R8/C2-4, plus establishing an MIH area. The project spans two sites along East 181st and 182nd Streets.
chapters.title: Applicant Walker-Stewart presents Sojourner Truth MAPES zoning actions

utterances.speaker: Astrid Walker-Stewart
utterances.text: Thank you, Matthew.

utterances.speaker: Astrid Walker-Stewart
utterances.text: So today we're going to be talking about two zoning map amendments and a zoning text amendment to facilitate a 100% affordable development and mixed-use development in the Cratona West Farms neighborhood

utterances.speaker: Astrid Walker-Stewart
utterances.text: in Council District 15, Community Board 6.

utterances.speaker: Astrid Walker-Stewart
utterances.text: So as you can see on the screen, the proposed project spans two sites along East 181st Street and East 182nd with Southern Boulevard and Cratona Parkway running through both sites.

utterances.speaker: Astrid Walker-Stewart
utterances.text: The first zoning map amendment we're proposing is to rezone the existing vacant site, Sojourner site, which is on the south of...

utterances.speaker: Astrid Walker-Stewart
utterances.text: On the screen from an R7-1 to an R8.

utterances.speaker: Astrid Walker-Stewart
utterances.text: And the second rezoning is to rezone the MAPES court site.

utterances.speaker: Astrid Walker-Stewart
utterances.text: So this would be phase two of our proposal to be constructed after the Sojourner site.

utterances.speaker: Astrid Walker-Stewart
utterances.text: And we are looking to rezone that site from an R7-1, C1-4 to R8, C2-4.

utterances.speaker: Astrid Walker-Stewart
utterances.text: You'll also note that the rezoning extends to the south of the MAPES court site.

utterances.speaker: Astrid Walker-Stewart
utterances.text: And this area was mapped with DCP's guidance.

utterances.speaker: Astrid Walker-Stewart
utterances.text: So they will also be rezoned from an R7-1, C1-4 to R8, C2-4.

utterances.speaker: Astrid Walker-Stewart
utterances.text: And then we're also looking to establish an MIH area as well.

utterances.speaker: Astrid Walker-Stewart
utterances.text: Next slide, please.

utterances.speaker: Astrid Walker-Stewart
utterances.text: So the project sits within, as you can see with the yellows and oranges, a predominantly residential neighborhood just south of the Bronx Zoo.

utterances.speaker: Astrid Walker-Stewart
utterances.text: This area is largely a mid-rise neighborhood with developments ranging in the height between two to eight stories to 14 stories and a 30-story tower to the south of the development site.

utterances.speaker: Astrid Walker-Stewart
utterances.text: Next slide, please.

utterances.speaker: Astrid Walker-Stewart
utterances.text: So the Sojourner site is currently a vacant site.

utterances.speaker: Astrid Walker-Stewart
utterances.text: It covers an entire block.

utterances.speaker: Astrid Walker-Stewart
utterances.text: And so we are excited to introduce housing to this vacant site.

utterances.speaker: Astrid Walker-Stewart
utterances.text: Next slide, please.

chapters.summary: Walker-Stewart presents the Sojourner site: 159 affordable units, 50% dedicated to MAPES tenants, 8-16 story building with concierge, maisonettes creating row-house scale, and landscaped rear yard. Height concentrated along the 100-foot-wide Southern Boulevard.

utterances.speaker: Astrid Walker-Stewart
utterances.text: And we are proposing, next slide.

utterances.speaker: Astrid Walker-Stewart
utterances.text: We're proposing 159 units of affordable housing on this site.

utterances.speaker: Astrid Walker-Stewart
utterances.text: As Matthew mentioned, 50% of these units will be dedicated to the MAPES tenants, so they will get a brand new building,

utterances.speaker: Astrid Walker-Stewart
utterances.text: amenities which they do not currently have, an elevator, and a landscape terrace, or a landscape area in the rear.

utterances.speaker: Astrid Walker-Stewart
utterances.text: The building ranges in height between 8 and 16 stories, and there is concierge on the ground floor at the corner, so tenants will be greeted upon entry.

utterances.speaker: Astrid Walker-Stewart
utterances.text: Next slide, please.

utterances.text: So this view showcases the massing of the project.

utterances.text: And so this creates a really nice human scale to the street and also gives tenants their own row house.

utterances.speaker: Astrid Walker-Stewart
utterances.text: And this view also highlights the landscape area in the rear yard.

utterances.speaker: Astrid Walker-Stewart
utterances.text: That is...

utterances.speaker: Astrid Walker-Stewart
utterances.text: accessible to tenants.

utterances.speaker: Astrid Walker-Stewart
utterances.text: Next slide, please.
